reading: The top 6x6 panel is a 3x3 pattern drawn at 2x scale; the bottom 6x6 panel (below the 5 separator) is a mask. The 18x18 output places one copy of the 3x3 pattern in every mask block whose mask cell is coloured, empty elsewhere.

slots.unit: top panel (above the full separator row) downscaled by 2 to 3x3
slots.mask: bottom panel (below the separator); a block gets a copy where the mask cell is non-background

why: output block (a,b) equals the downscaled pattern iff mask cell (a,b) is non-background, else all background
invariants: mask colour never appears in output

reading: Every isolated 5 is replaced by a fixed 3x3 stamp 515/101/515 centred on it (the centre becomes 0).
why: each marker cell is the centre of one identical 3x3 copy; no other cells are coloured
invariants: marker positions are the stamp centres

reading: Each non-background grid corner holds a colour c. Every 5x5 shape that contains a c cell swaps its two colours (main colour <-> c), and the union of all those shapes' masks is drawn in colour c in a 5x5 box flush against that corner.
verb: swap colours and gather shapes at corner

slots.key_colour: colour of each non-background grid corner cell
slots.subjects: shapes (5x5 boxes, possibly not connected) containing a cell of the key colour
slots.recolour: within each subject, main colour <-> key colour
slots.stamp: union of the subject masks, box aligned to the matching grid corner, painted in the key colour

why: for each corner colour c, the shapes holding c are colour-swapped and their overlaid silhouettes appear at the corner of colour c
invariants: shapes without a corner colour unchanged

reading: A lattice of framed boxes, most with the common centre colour; boxes with a rare centre colour are linked: every background cell lying on a row or column between two rare cells of the same colour is filled with that colour.

new_rows.name: link
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
top(max(N)) :- ccount(C, N).
low(N) :- ccount(C, N), top(T), N < T.
second(max(N)) :- low(N).
special(C) :- ccount(C, N), second(S), N < S.
sp(Y, X, C) :- cell(Y, X, C), special(C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
link(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), sp(Y, X1, C), sp(Y, X2, C), X1 < X, X < X2.
link(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), sp(Y1, X, C), sp(Y2, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.

why: only background cells between two same-colour rare-centre cells on a row/column change, taking that colour; frames and other centres stay
invariants: all box frames and centres unchanged

reading: The grid is symmetric (left-right, up-down and transpose); patches painted 4 hide parts of it and are restored from their mirror images.
why: the output is fully symmetric and only cells that were 4 in the input change

reading: A cup at the bottom: base row A..BBB..A with a top bar above the B part. From the cells diagonally above-outside the top bar's two ends, diagonal lines in the base's middle colour B run up-left and up-right to the border.

slots.sources: the two ends of the second-from-bottom bar
slots.direction: up-left from the left end, up-right from the right end (diagonal)
slots.colour: the middle colour of the bottom row (not the bar's colour)

why: each diagonal starts one step diagonally outside a bar end and reaches the border; nothing else changes

reading: The input is a row of identical framed panels showing one small shape that moves vertically by a step from panel to panel; the output is one panel with the shape at the next position in the sequence.

slots.panels: stripes cut by full separator columns
slots.subject: the small shape inside each panel
slots.output: one panel, shape at last position + step

why: output = a single panel whose shape position continues the panels' motion (pair 1 lands one row further than a constant step predicts)

reading: Every 4 in a column whose index is a multiple of 3 becomes 6.

new_rows.name: third
new_rows.datalog:
third(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
third(Y, X2) :- third(Y, X), X2 = X + 3, px(Y, X2, C).

why: cells in columns 0,3,6,... map 4->6 (0 stays); all other cells unchanged

reading: Left 4x4 panel is a 1-shape with holes, right 4x4 panel a coloured piece. If the piece exactly occupies the holes (same position), the output is the left panel with holes filled by the piece; otherwise the output is the left panel unchanged.

slots.condition: piece cells == base hole cells exactly, no shift
slots.result: overlay piece on base if condition holds, else base

why: output is always the left panel, with the right panel's colours overlaid exactly when they match the holes

reading: Two 2 cells lie on one row, column or diagonal; every cell on the straight line between them is recoloured: 0 becomes 2 and 1 becomes 3.

new_rows.name: seg
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2.
seg(Y, X) :- two(Y, X1), two(Y, X2), X1 < X, X < X2, px(Y, X, C).
seg(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X), two(Y2, X), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, px(Y, X, C).
seg(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X1), two(Y2, X2), Y1 < Y2, E = Y2 - Y1, F = X2 - X1, F = E, px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, DY = Y - Y1, DX = X - X1, DX = DY.
seg(Y, X) :- two(Y1, X1), two(Y2, X2), Y1 < Y2, E = Y2 - Y1, G = X1 - X2, G = E, px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, DY = Y - Y1, DX = X1 - X, DX = DY.

why: only cells strictly between the two 2s on their shared line change, by 0->2 and 1->3
